blocks.text: Short answer, because you've probably got a kick-off time to make: for a proper big-game atmosphere in Bondi we head to the [Beach Road Hotel](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/beach-road-hotel) - two storeys, four island bars and a beer garden that fills up fast for State of Origin and grand finals. For cheaper schooners, ocean views and a family-friendly room where the kids are welcome for an afternoon game, the local clubs are unbeatable: [North Bondi RSL](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/north-bondi-rsl), the [Bondi Bowlo](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bondi-bowlo-bondi-bowling-club) and the [Bondi Golf & Diggers Club](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bondi-golf-and-diggers-club). Below is how we actually choose, sport by sport and occasion by occasion.

items.label: Biggest atmosphere
items.value: Beach Road Hotel (beer garden, multiple bars)

items.label: Best ocean-view sport
items.value: North Bondi RSL, Bondi Golf & Diggers Club

items.label: Golden rule
items.value: Call the venue to confirm your exact game is on

blocks.text: One thing up front, and we mean it: **broadcast rights and what's on which screen change constantly**, and no Bondi venue shows every code on every screen. NRL, AFL, the cricket, Wallabies and Wallaroos Tests, State of Origin and the big international events all sit across different broadcasters and pay-TV packages. So treat this as a guide to the **rooms**, not a promise about a specific fixture. Before you walk down, ring ahead or check the venue's socials and ask them to confirm they're putting your game on. It saves the heartbreak of arriving to find the room locked onto something else.
The pubs and hotels for the big games
Beach Road Hotel - our all-rounder

If we could only send you to one place, it's the Beach Road Hotel on the corner of Beach Road and Roscoe Street. It's a big, two-level pub with four island bars, a dog-friendly beer garden and an upstairs courtyard, which is exactly what you want for a rowdy Origin night or an NRL or AFL grand final - plenty of room, plenty of screens and a crowd that's actually into it. It's the natural pick for a **big group** because you can spread out and still all see a screen. Because it's popular, get there early for the marquee fixtures, and confirm with them that your specific match is going up before you commit.
Hotel Bondi and The Royal Bondi

Up on Campbell Parade, the grand old [Hotel Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/hotel-bondi) is a classic beachfront pub with several bars across the building, so it's a solid fallback if the Beachy is heaving. A short walk up Bondi Road, [The Royal Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/the-royal-bondi) is a proper local's pub - more neighbourhood corner-pub than mega sports bar, but a good spot to settle in with a beer and a counter meal for a rugby Test or a session of the cricket. As always, both change their sport programming match to match, so a quick call is the move.
A beachfront beer with the game on

For something more bar than barn, [Hotel Ravesis](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/hotel-ravesis) on the beachfront and the [Bondi Beach Public Bar](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bondi-beach-public-bar) on Campbell Parade are relaxed places to catch a game over a drink rather than scream at a twelve-metre screen. They suit a lower-key afternoon - a Wallabies Test, a T20, an afternoon of the Ashes - more than a packed-out Origin decider. Want to browse the full drinks-first list? Here's our roundup of the [best bars in Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/best-bars-bondi-beach).
The clubs: cheaper beers, ocean views and family-friendly rooms

Bondi's licensed clubs are, honestly, an underrated way to watch sport. Sign in (visitors are welcome, bring photo ID), the drinks are usually cheaper than the pubs, the bistro meals are good value, and the rooms tend to be brighter and more relaxed - which makes them the easy call for a **day game with kids**.
North Bondi RSL

North Bondi RSL sits right above the sand at the north end with some of the best free ocean views in the suburb, big screens in the bar and TAB area, and a family-friendly bistro. It's our go-to for an afternoon fixture where you want the footy on, a parma in front of you and space for the family. Genuinely one of the nicest rooms in Bondi to watch anything, and the value is hard to beat.
Bondi Bowlo and Bondi Golf & Diggers Club

The Bondi Bowlo (the Bondi Bowling Club) is all easy-going, open-air charm - greens, a beer garden and a laid-back crowd. It's more of a casual, sunny-arvo spot than a wall of screens, so check what they've got showing before a night game, but for a relaxed weekend fixture with a group it's a joy. Perched on the clifftop walk toward the northern headland, the Bondi Golf & Diggers Club is another casual club option with a bistro, a friendly bar and a view - a lovely, low-key place to catch a game away from the crush. For more sit-down options with the sport on, browse our [best pubs in Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink/pubs-bondi-beach).
Which venue for which occasion

items: **State of Origin / NRL & AFL grand finals** - big atmosphere, big crowd: Beach Road Hotel first, Hotel Bondi as backup. Arrive early.
**Rugby union Tests (Wallabies/Wallaroos) & internationals** - The Royal Bondi or Hotel Ravesis for a settled, less frantic watch.
**Cricket (Ashes, BBL, ODIs)** - long-format days suit the clubs and beachfront bars where you can graze and stay a while.
**A day game with the family** - [North Bondi RSL](/bondi-eat-and-drink/family-friendly-bondi-beach) and the Bondi Bowlo: welcoming, good-value, kid-friendly.
**Big group / stag-and-hens energy** - Beach Road Hotel's multiple bars and beer garden give everyone room to move.

blocks.text: For a marquee night like Origin, don't just check that a venue shows sport in general - message them that day and confirm they're putting the actual game on the main screen, and ask whether they're taking bookings or running a minimum spend for tables. The good rooms fill up hours before kick-off.

blocks.title: Hungry before kick-off?
blocks.text: Every venue here sits inside our full, searchable Bondi eat-and-drink directory - with menus, locations and what each place is best for. Line your stomach, then find your screen: browse the whole [Bondi eat & drink guide](/bondi-eat-and-drink).
Watching the football (soccer) too?

If it's the Premier League, Champions League or a European fixture you're chasing rather than the footy codes, we've written a separate companion guide: [where to watch English football in Bondi](/bondi-blog/2025/5/25/where-to-watch-english-football-in-bondi-the-best-pubs-and-bars-for-premier-league-fans). Late kick-offs and early-hours European games are a different beast, and that piece covers the pubs and bars that stay open for them.

items.q: Where's the best place to watch the NRL in Bondi?
items.a: For atmosphere on a big night, the [Beach Road Hotel](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/beach-road-hotel). For a cheaper, family-friendly afternoon game, [North Bondi RSL](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/north-bondi-rsl) or the [Bondi Bowlo](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/bondi-bowlo-bondi-bowling-club). Always confirm the exact match is on before you head down.

items.q: Where can I watch State of Origin in Bondi?
items.a: The Beach Road Hotel and Hotel Bondi draw the biggest Origin crowds; the local clubs are the relaxed, better-value alternative. It's a huge night everywhere, so get in early and check whether the venue is taking bookings.

items.q: Is there a proper sports bar in Bondi?
items.a: Bondi leans more towards pubs and clubs than dedicated sports bars. The Beach Road Hotel is the closest to a full sports-bar experience with its multiple bars, screens and beer garden.

items.q: Can I take kids to watch the game?
items.a: Yes - the licensed clubs are your best bet. North Bondi RSL and the Bondi Bowlo have family-friendly bistros and daytime hours that suit an afternoon fixture. Check each venue's minors policy for evening games.

items.q: Will a venue definitely be showing my game?
items.a: Never assume. Broadcast rights and screen line-ups change constantly and no venue shows every code. Ring ahead or check their socials on the day and ask them to confirm.

blocks.text: That's the local's shortlist. Bondi isn't a suburb of cavernous sports bars - it's pubs with history and clubs with a view - and that's the charm of watching a game here: sea air, cold schooner, and a room full of people who care as much as you do. Pick your venue, confirm your fixture, get there before kick-off, and enjoy it. See you at the bar.
